classification.difficultyReason: Must construct an exhaustive set of repetition patterns, respect which letters can be doubled or tripled and assign the correct selection and permutation factors.

content.prompt: How many six-letter codes can be made from the letters of the word STATISTICAL?

answer.short:
$16\,680$ codes.

Add the six possible repetition-pattern cases, dividing each permutation count by the factorials of repeated letters.
answer.worked:
The available letters are T three times; S, A and I twice each; and C and L once each. Classify codes by their letter multiplicities. There are four letter types that can be doubled, but only T can be tripled.

Triple, double and single:
$$\begin{align*}N_{3,2,1}&=\binom{3}{1}\binom{4}{1}\frac{6!}{3!2!}\\N_{3,2,1}&=720.\end{align*}$$

Triple and three distinct singles:
$$\begin{align*}N_{3,1,1,1}&=\binom{5}{3}\frac{6!}{3!}\\N_{3,1,1,1}&=1200.\end{align*}$$

Three doubles:
$$\begin{align*}N_{2,2,2}&=\binom{4}{3}\frac{6!}{(2!)^3}\\N_{2,2,2}&=360.\end{align*}$$

Two doubles and two distinct singles:
$$\begin{align*}N_{2,2,1,1}&=\binom{4}{2}\binom{4}{2}\frac{6!}{(2!)^2}\\N_{2,2,1,1}&=6480.\end{align*}$$

One double and four distinct singles:
$$\begin{align*}N_{2,1,1,1,1}&=\binom{4}{1}\binom{5}{4}\frac{6!}{2!}\\N_{2,1,1,1,1}&=7200.\end{align*}$$

Six distinct letters:
$$\begin{align*}N_{1,1,1,1,1,1}&=6!\\N_{1,1,1,1,1,1}&=720.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}N&=720+1200+360+6480+7200+720\\N&=16\,680.\end{align*}$$
